title: Freehand Drawing
subtitle: Studies in Blackness and Tone
summary: Charcoal studies after Kollwitz, Redon, Daumier and Rego, treating black not as absence but as weight and presence.
description: This body of work began as a study of master drawings. I closely observed and reinterpreted the techniques of artists such as Käthe Kollwitz, Odilon Redon, and others whose work expresses emotional depth through tonal intensity. I focused on how blackness, both as a material and as a concept, could be constructed through accumulated marks.

In early studies, I examined how shadows were not simply filled areas, but spaces slowly built up through smudging, layering, and erasure. Each technique introduced a different texture, and each texture altered the quality of darkness in the narrative. As I moved into composition, I began thinking of black not as absence, but as weight and presence, pulling focus and creating contrast. I layered different strategies together, often revisiting a single area over and over to create depth across different levels of grey.
